source_caption_text:
Nothing could’ve prepared me for hearing this for the first time 🤒🔥

50 Cent’s “Many Men” is one of the standout tracks from his 2003 debut album, Get Rich or D*e Tryin’. Built around a dark piano loop and slow, heavy production, the song has a completely different feel from a typical rap hit of that era. 50 uses the track to talk about surviving being shot nine times, the people who wanted him gone, and the paranoia that came with everything he had been through.

The hook is what makes the song instantly recognizable. 50’s delivery is calm but filled with emotion as he raps about death, betrayal, violence, and trying to survive despite everything working against him. There’s a real sense of vulnerability throughout the song, which helped separate “Many Men” from the more aggressive records on Get Rich or D*e Tryin’.

More than 20 years later, “Many Men” is still one of 50 Cent’s most recognizable songs and has become a major part of hip-hop culture. The record has been referenced, sampled, and reworked by artists including Pop Smoke and 21 Savage, while the original continues to connect with new generations of rap fans. It’s one of those songs that became bigger than its original release and remains closely tied to 50 Cent’s story.
